newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices hit new year-highs.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices hit new year-highs.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices continued to rally Thursday to reach the highest levels of the year as traders faced bitterly cold weather, a plant outage in British Columbia and pipeline balancing penalties.

At Sumas, Wash., the Canada-U.S. export point, prices for Friday delivery rose by about $1 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) to about $5, with some distressed deals confirmed done early as high as $10.
Propping up the market early was news that Westcoast Energy was cutting more than 300 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas flows due to a late Wednesday outage at the McMahon plant in B.C.
The company said it expected to restore full service from its current 50 percent power level this Saturday. The plant's capacity is about 650 mmcfd.
Also influencing the market, traders said, is the issuance of load balancing penalties by Northwest Pipeline.
If a shipper is eight percent over the pipeline's tolerance, a $5 per mmBtu penalty is issued, while 10 percent over results in a $10 charge, one trader said.

At the AECO storage hub, prices began around C$2.80 per gigajoule (GJ) but softened throughout Thursday's session to the mid-C$2.40s. Most deals were confirmed done near C$2.70, which is unchanged from Wednesday.

With the McMahon outage likely to continue through Friday and cold temperatures forecast to linger in western Canada through at least the early part of next week, many traders expected Canadian domestic prices to remain strong in the near-term.
However, following the restoration of service on Westcoast, most traders said they expect prices to soften at Sumas.
December Sumas prices were talked in the mid-$3 area.
At Niagara, where colder temperatures are forecast through next week, prices gained about 30 cents on the day to the $4.05-4.10 per mmBtu range.
